The cause is clear:

1. The 4.3.0 deployment added `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` to the security context (compare with the 4.2 pods which don't have this setting).
2. Next.js tries to create the directory `/app/.next/cache` at startup.
3. With `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, the filesystem is read-only and that `mkdir` call fails with `EROFS: read-only file system`.
4. This causes the process to exit with code 1, triggering CrashLoopBackOff.

The fix is to mount an `emptyDir` volume at `/app/.next/cache` so Next.js can write to it even with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
I should look up more documentation on emptyDir volumes to cite the right reference.
